Research Question: Which customer segments have the highest churn risk?

Additional Questions 1. Which subscription plans are most associated with customer churn? 2. What customer behaviors serve as strong predictors of churn? 3. Can we build a predictive model for churn?

Dictionary customerID - ID number of customer gender - if customer is male/female SeniorCitizen - if customer is senior citizen Partner - if customer has a partner Dependents - if customer has dependents tenure - # of months customer has used the service PhoneService - if customer has phone service MultipleLines - if customer has multiple lines (yes=they have multiple lines, no=they don’t have multiple lines, no phone service=might have multiple lines but no phone service, or might not have multiple lines and have no phone service) InternetService - if customer has internet service OnlineSecurity - if they have online security OnlineBackup - if they have online backup DeviceProtection - if they have device protection TechSupport - if customer has tech support StreamingTV - if customer has tv streaming StreamingMovies - if customer has movie streaming Contract - contract term of the customer (month-to-month, 1 yr, 2 yr) PaperlessBilling - if they have paperless billing PaymentMethod - customer’s payment method MonthlyCharges - amount charged to customer monthly TotalCharges - total amount charged to customer Churn - whether the customer churned or not

Drop all the “no internet service” appearances in the dataset

telco[telco == "No internet service"] <- NA

Convert non-numeric data to binary

#Key services

#Phone service
telco$PSbin <- NA
telco$PSbin[telco$PhoneService == "Yes"] <- 1
telco$PSbin[telco$PhoneService == "No"] <- 0

#Internet Service
telco$ISbin <- ifelse(telco$InternetService == "No", 0, 1)

#TV streaming
telco$STbin <- NA
telco$STbin[telco$StreamingTV == "Yes"] <- 1
telco$STbin[telco$StreamingTV == "No"] <- 0

#Movie streaming
telco$SMbin <- NA
telco$SMbin[telco$StreamingMovies == "Yes"] <- 1
telco$SMbin[telco$StreamingMovies == "No"] <- 0

#Online security
telco$OSbin <- NA
telco$OSbin[telco$OnlineSecurity == "Yes"] <- 1
telco$OSbin[telco$OnlineSecurity == "No"] <- 0

#Online backup
telco$OBbin <- NA
telco$OBbin[telco$OnlineBackup == "Yes"] <- 1
telco$OBbin[telco$OnlineBackup == "No"] <- 0

#Device protection
telco$DPbin <- NA
telco$DPbin[telco$DeviceProtection == "Yes"] <- 1
telco$DPbin[telco$DeviceProtection == "No"] <- 0

Other variables to control for

#Key variable (churn)
telco$Chbin <- NA
telco$Chbin[telco$Churn == "Yes"] <- 1
telco$Chbin[telco$Churn == "No"] <- 0

#Many lines
telco$MLbin <- NA
telco$MLbin[telco$MultipleLines == "Yes"] <- 1
telco$MLbin[telco$MultipleLines == "No"] <- 0
telco$MLbin[telco$MultipleLines == "No phone service"] <- NA

#Tech support
telco$TSbin <- NA
telco$TSbin[telco$TechSupport == "Yes"] <- 1
telco$TSbin[telco$TechSupport == "No"] <- 0

#Gender, male/female
telco$Gbin <- NA
telco$Gbin[telco$gender == "Male"] <- 1
telco$Gbin[telco$gender == "Female"] <- 0

#Contract length
telco$Cbin <- NA
telco$Cbin[telco$Contract == "Month-to-month"] <- 2
telco$Cbin[telco$Contract == "One year"] <- 1
telco$Cbin[telco$Contract == "Two year"] <- 0

#Paperless billing
telco$PBbin <- NA
telco$PBbin[telco$PaperlessBilling == "Yes"] <- 1
telco$PBbin[telco$PaperlessBilling == "No"] <- 0

#Payment methods
telco$Paybin <- NA
telco$Paybin[telco$PaymentMethod == "Electronic Check"] <- 2
telco$Paybin[telco$PaymentMethod == "Mailed Check"] <- 1
telco$Paybin[telco$PaymentMethod == "Bank transfer (automatic)"] <- 0

Which subscription plans are most associated with customer churn? There are 7 types of service: phone, tv, movies, internet, and 3 device protections

#Compare variables with each to see significance
#Make tables of variables to compare

#Phone service, churn
PCHtab <- table(telco$PSbin, telco$Chbin)
#Internet service, churn
IStab <- table(telco$ISbin, telco$Chbin)
#TV streaming, churn
STtab <- table(telco$STbin, telco$Chbin)
#Movie streaming, churn
SMtab <- table(telco$SMbin, telco$Chbin)
#Online security
OStab <- table(telco$OnlineSecurity, telco$Chbin)
#Online backup
OBtab <- table(telco$OnlineBackup, telco$Chbin)
#Device protection
DPtab <- table(telco$DeviceProtection, telco$Chbin)
#Run correlation with psych library
phi(PCHtab, 3)
## [1] 0.012
phi(IStab, 3)
## [1] 0.228
phi(STtab, 3)
## [1] -0.037
phi(SMtab, 3)
## [1] -0.04
phi(OStab, 3)
## [1] -0.281
phi(OBtab, 3)
## [1] -0.196
phi(DPtab, 3)
## [1] -0.177

It appears that phone service with churn and internet service with churn have positive correlations. Streaming movies and streaming tv with churn has a negative correlation.

Now that correlations have been run, regression models can be run to find significance.

TV streaming has a negative correlation with churn. Its significant, but not as much as internet service and churn. The p-value is 0.0591. If a customer has the tv-streaming service, then they are 3% more likely to churn (leave the service). About a 1/3 (33%) would leave the service. Later we can check to see what causes this churn rate, such as high monthly bills or contract length.

After analyzing the churn rate with various streaming services, the service with the highest churn rate is movie streaming with -0.037390. There’s a high likelihood that customers will quit their movie streaming service compared to other services. So the subscription plan with the highest churn risk is movie streaming.

Now we can answer the 2nd additional question of: What customer behaviors serve as strong predictors of churn?
After analyzing the above data with linear regressions, we can see that customers that have internet service are statistically more likely to churn compared to those without internet service. Customers that have protective services, such as online backup, online security, or device protection, or less likely to churn that those that don’t have it. So internet service serves as a strong positive predictor of churn, and online seucirty, online backup, and device protection serves as strong negative predictors of churn. 
#We can run an initial correlation between the contract table and the monthly charges variable. 
#It seems to have a positive correlation, but is it significant?
cor(telco$MonthlyCharges, telco$Cbin)
## [1] 0.07419467

It appears that contract length does attribute to a high churn rate.

#Churn compared with monthly charges and contract length
#Does contract length correlate with high monthly charges? If so, does this contribute to a high churn rate?
#Create a plot with each of the 3 contract length categories showing the monthly charges. (month-to-month, 1 yr, 2 yr)

Tech Support and Multiple Lines weren’t included because I want to see later on if the availability of tech support by itself has an effect on churn rates, independent of all other variables. Multiple Lines wasn’t included because I don’t know what’s included in the variable Multiple Lines. Adding all of the services together with contract length was easier to see the relationships between each other.

When all of the services are added with contract length, surprisingly Streaming TV and Streaming Movies is the least significant. Device Protection and Phone Service dropped a little in significance as well.

I want to look a little further into internet service with contract length to try and see which individual service has the highest churn rate.

## F-statistic:   483 on 4 and 7038 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16

In comparison to DSL, Fiber Optic is 0.17 percentage points more likely to churn. Having no internet service is 0.06 percentage points more likely to stay? (Reinterpret)

The third and final question we can answer is: Can we build a predictive model for churn?

The answer will be binary, either yes or no. This means we can use a logistic regression to interpret the results.
Some good machine learning models that would’ve been ideal are random forest or a chi square test. But we can just create a linear predictive model by running a logistic regression model with some of the variables. We can add almost all of the variables we want to look (services) to see how the logistic model affects it. We can look at Gaussian and binomial to compare.

#Can we build a predictive model for churn?

#Churn with Internet Service, TV Streaming, Movie Streaming, Online Service, Online Backup, Device Protection
m10 <- glm(Chbin ~ ISbin + STbin + SMbin + OSbin + OBbin + DPbin, family = c("binomial"), data = telco)
summary(m10)

telco_clean <- na.omit(telco)

#telco$predict_prob <- predict(m10, type = "response")
#Telco clean
m11 <- glm(Chbin ~ ISbin + STbin + SMbin + OSbin + OBbin + DPbin, family = c("binomial"), data = telco_clean)
summary(m11)

## Call:

##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)

## STbin         0.1075     0.1807   0.595 0.551924    
## SMbin         0.1482     0.1807   0.820 0.411984

## OBbin        -0.6768     0.1628  -4.156 3.23e-05 ***

#Predict churn probabilities
telco_clean$predicted_prob <- predict(m11, type = "response")

#This determines a cutoff threshold
telco_clean$predicted_class <- ifelse(telco_clean$predicted_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)

These lines of code predict churn probabilities and determines a cutoff threshold. If the probability is > 0.5, then this means “will churn”. If the probability is <= 0.5, then is “won’t churn”. We can now look at the dataset and see the new columns that are made. Chbin is original churn, predicted_prob is the model’s estimated probability and predicted_class is the model’s choice (if it churned or not). So yes, a predictive model can be made for churn.

hist(telco_clean$predicted_prob, 
     breaks = 20,
     main = "Predicted Churn Probabilities",
     xlab = "Probability of Churn",
     col = "lightblue",
     border = "black")

abline(v = 0.5, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)  #vertical line at 0.5
